From bb73d5d9164c57c4bb916739a98e5cd8e0a5ed8c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Aug 2022 13:28:37 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] iio: adc: at91-sama5d2_adc: fix AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX

All ADC HW versions handled by this driver (SAMA5D2, SAM9X60, SAMA7G5)
have MR.TRACKTIM on 4 bits. Fix AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX to reflect
this.

Fixes: 27e177190891 ("iio:adc:at91_adc8xx: introduce new atmel adc driver")
Signed-off-by: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220803102855.2191070-2-claudiu.beznea@microchip.com
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>

diff --git a/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c b/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c
index 279430c1d88c..ac9ef89fba17 100644
--- a/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c
+++ b/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c
@@ -77,7 +77,7 @@ struct at91_adc_reg_layout {
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_ANACH		BIT(23)
 /* Tracking Time */
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM(v)	((v) << 24)
-#define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX	0xff
+#define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX	0xf
 /* Transfer Time */
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRANSFER(v)	((v) << 28)
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRANSFER_MAX	0x3
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c`**
   - The definition of `AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX` was changed from `0xff` to `0xf`. This modification reflects that all ADC hardware versions handled by this driver (SAMA5D2, SAM9X60, SAMA7G5) have the `MR.TRACKTIM` field represented with 4 bits.

### Relationships

- The change in the `AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX` constant is a bug fix that ensures the maximum value for the tracking time is correctly defined according to the hardware specifications. This fix is related to the previous commit identified by the hash `27e177190891`, which introduced the new Atmel ADC driver. The modification corrects an oversight in that introduction, aligning the code with the actual hardware capabilities.

Here is the commit message:
iio: adc: at91-sama5d2_adc: fix AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX

All ADC HW versions handled by this driver (SAMA5D2, SAM9X60, SAMA7G5)
have MR.TRACKTIM on 4 bits. Fix AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX to reflect
this.

Fixes: 27e177190891 ("iio:adc:at91_adc8xx: introduce new atmel adc driver")
Signed-off-by: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220803102855.2191070-2-claudiu.beznea@microchip.com
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect definition of the `AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX` constant, which was set to `0xff` instead of the correct value `0xf`. This misrepresentation did not accurately reflect the 4-bit capability of the `MR.TRACKTIM` field for the ADC hardware versions supported by the driver, leading to potential misconfigurations or incorrect behavior when setting tracking time values.

Here is the patch:
 /* Tracking Time */
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM(v)	((v) << 24)
-#define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX	0xff
+#define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX	0xf
 /* Transfer Time */
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRANSFER(v)	((v) << 28)

Reason:
The constant `AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX` was incorrectly defined as `0xff`, which represents an 8-bit value (255) instead of the correct 4-bit maximum value. This misrepresentation could lead to incorrect configurations when setting the tracking time for the ADC, potentially causing the hardware to behave unexpectedly.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

#define AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX 0xf
